data.name: Chidambar
data.gender_notes: Chidambar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is referred to as Chidambar. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘chid’ meaning sky and ‘ambar’ meaning to wear. It signifies the deity being dressed in the sky. The name Chidambar carries the meaning “Sky-clad, wearing the sky” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chidambar usually hope their child will grow to embody sky-clad, wearing the sky and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine presence of Lord Shiva, who embodies the universe.
data.etymology: Chidambar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sky-clad, wearing the sky.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chidambar total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chidambar holds immense significance in Indian culture and is considered as one of the most sacred places in Hinduism. The Chidambaram Natarajar Temple in Tamil Nadu, India, is famed for the thousand pillared hall, where Lord Shiva is depicted in the form of Nataraja or Lord of Dance. The annual dance festival held here is a major pilgrimage for devotees and serves as a testament to the rich cultural heritage of India.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is worshipped as the supreme spiritual teacher. The name Chidambar reiterates the idea of the deity residing in the infinite sky, beyond the tangible world. Devotees believe that through contemplating upon the form of Lord Shiva in the cosmic dance (Tandava) depicted in this name, they can attain salvation and mystical experiences. It is a reminder of the spiritual truth that the ultimate reality (Brahman) transcends the material world and dwells within the infinite expanse of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Chidambar means 'the limitless sky' or 'the pure and radiant space'. It symbolizes the infinite and divine consciousness that pervades the universe. In Hinduism, Chidambar is often associated with Lord Shiva, representing the pure, unmanifested form of the divine.

historical_references.reference: Chidambaram Temple, one of the most ancient and renowned Shiva temples in India, is located in the town of Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu. The temple is believed to have originated in the 2nd century AD, although its present structure is largely a result of later renovations and additions. The name 'Chidambaram' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'chid' (consciousness), 'ambara' (sky or heaven) and 'ram' (resides), meaning 'the one who resides in the pure consciousness of the sky'. The temple is famous for its unique architectural design and its association with the Agama texts.

Another reference to the name 'Chidambaram' can be found in the Puranic literature, specifically in the Agni Purana. It is mentioned that Lord Shiva, in his form as Nataraja, performed the cosmic dance in the town of Chidambaram. The name 'Chidambaram' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'chid' (consciousness), 'ambara' (sky or heaven), and 'ram' (resides), implying that Lord Shiva resides in the pure consciousness of the sky. The temple at Chidambaram is believed to be the spiritual center for the worship of Lord Nataraja.

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
